titleBack: You Know Who I Answer To

flipToBack.timing: Required after-triggers, two independent routes: (A) event trigger justHitBy at any time; (B) isTableChanged gated to YOUR battle phase.
flipToBack.prose: Route A: flip when a character was just 'hit' by your card (any character, any location; no canBeFlipped guard in code). Route B: flip during your battle phase when your gangsters CONTROL two battlegrounds (controlsWith). On the resulting flip, front's cardFlipped trigger makes opponent lose 1 Force if you occupy 3 battlegrounds.

children.req: timing trigger: character just 'hit' by your card
controlsWith: control 2 battlegrounds with actor there

flipToFront.timing: Required after-trigger at end of EACH turn (automatic, singleton) - the back never persists across a turn boundary.
flipToFront.prose: Flips back at end of every turn (TriggerConditions.isEndOfEachTurn), unconditional (no canBeFlipped guard in code). Companion effects: on flipping (cardFlipped on back) owner MAY re-circulate and shuffle Reserve Deck; on the back-to-front flip the FRONT's cardFlipped trigger fires - if you occupy 3 battlegrounds, opponent loses 1 Force.

expression.req: timing trigger: end of each turn

requirementSemantics: flipToBack route A: pure event trigger (your card just hit a character) - no board-state requirement, no canBeFlipped check
flipToBack route B: CONTROL-with (2 battlegrounds with a gangster there) + phase gate (your battle phase only)
flipToFront: unconditional end-of-turn timing trigger - this objective oscillates; the back is a one-turn buff window

profile.frontRule: controlWith two battlegrounds using distinct non-undercover gangsters during the owner's battle phase
deliberateRuntimeBoundaries: Route A is a transient justHitBy event, so it is executed through exact native pull support and existing legal weapon-fire logic rather than represented as a persistent playbook rule.
The back flips front unconditionally at end of every turn, so no postFlip hold rule exists.
The three-battleground clause is a one-shot native Force-loss rider, not a hold rule.
